quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #8
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: What do speed limit signs show?

options.text: Possible speeds for the area
The highest or lowest speed you are allowed to drive
The speed to drive in heavy traffic
The speed to drive in bad weather

questions.correctAnswerText: The highest or lowest speed you are allowed to drive
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs show the highest or lowest safe speed allowed on a road. The highest limits are for perfect conditions. You must slow down when conditions are worse.

questions.question: Driving while distracted:

options.text: Is never dangerous.
Usually makes drivers react slower to hazards.
Usually makes drivers go faster.
Is only dangerous for young drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually makes drivers react slower to hazards.
questions.explanation: Distractions slow down how fast a driver can react to traffic and dangers on the road. Distracted driving is always unsafe.

questions.question: An "End school zone" sign means:

options.text: The speed limit is now 20 mph.
A reduced speed zone is starting.
More pedestrians may be near.
A reduced speed zone is ending.

questions.correctAnswerText: A reduced speed zone is ending.
questions.explanation: Do not go faster than the school zone speed limit during the times shown. An "End school zone" sign shows where the reduced speed zone ends.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a hill with a curb:

options.text: Turn your front wheels sharply toward the curb.
Turn your front wheels slightly to the right.
Turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb.
Keep your front wheels straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb.
questions.explanation: Turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb to stop your car from rolling into traffic. On streets with no curb, turn the wheels sharply toward the edge of the road.

questions.question: When someone is tailgating you:

options.text: Move to the right lane if it is open.
If no right lane is open, wait until the road ahead is clear and slow down gradually to let the tailgater pass.
Never brake hard suddenly.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating and a right lane is open, move over. If no right lane is open, wait until the road is clear ahead and then slow down gradually to let them pass. Never brake hard suddenly, as this increases the risk of being hit from behind.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Steep grade ahead.
Pedestrian crossing ahead.
Low ground railroad crossing.
Low clearance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low clearance.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the overpass ahead has low clearance. Do not continue if your vehicle is taller than the height shown on the sign (13 feet 6 inches in this case).

questions.question: You must be extra careful when driving near a pedestrian with a white cane because:

options.text: He or she is deaf.
He or she is a police officer.
He or she is blind.
He or she has poor balance.

questions.correctAnswerText: He or she is blind.
questions.explanation: When you see a blind person with a white cane or guide dog, slow down, give them the right of way, and proceed with caution. Be ready to stop to protect them.

questions.question: This sign is a:

options.text: Service sign.
Regulatory sign.
Warning sign.
Stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning sign.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped and yellow with black letters or pictures. They warn drivers about special situations or dangers ahead.

questions.question: When passing a parked vehicle on the side of the road, drivers should:

options.text: Speed up.
Move to the far lane away from the parked vehicle or slow down.
Pull off the road behind the parked vehicle.
Move to the lane closest to the parked vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the far lane away from the parked vehicle or slow down.
questions.explanation: The Move Over Law protects police officers, emergency workers, tow truck drivers, sanitation workers, and utility workers on the road. You must move away from stopped emergency vehicles, tow trucks, sanitation vehicles, or utility vehicles. If you cannot move over safely, slow down to 20 mph below the posted speed limit.

questions.question: You must make way for emergency vehicles:

options.text: Never.
When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.
Only when other vehicles do.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.
questions.explanation: You must give the right of way to any emergency vehicle using a siren or flashing lights.

questions.question: When may you carefully continue through an intersection on a yellow light?

options.text: When an emergency vehicle is crossing your lane.
When pedestrians are crossing.
When you are turning right.
When you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow.
questions.explanation: If the light turns yellow while you are already in the intersection, you may continue through carefully.

questions.question: When may you cross double solid yellow lines?

options.text: To pass a slow-moving truck.
To turn into a driveway.
To pass another car.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: To turn into a driveway.
questions.explanation: Double solid lines mean you cannot pass or change lanes. You may only cross them to turn into or out of a driveway or to make a U-turn where permitted.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Pedestrians are walking along the road ahead.
A pedestrian crossing is ahead.
Pedestrians cannot cross here.
Construction workers are on the road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A pedestrian crossing is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a pedestrian crossing is ahead. Be careful and watch for people crossing the road.

questions.question: Which substances can impair your driving and result in a DUII arrest?

options.text: Beer, wine, and other alcohol
Illegal drugs or prescription medicines
Inhalants such as glue or paint
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: Many substances can impair your driving, including alcohol, illegal drugs, prescription medicines, over-the-counter medicines, and inhalants.

questions.question: What should you do to prevent fatigue on a long trip?

options.text: Stop and rest every two hours.
Do arm exercises every hour.
Drive with one eye open at a time.
Alternate which foot you use on the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest every two hours.
questions.explanation: Stop every two hours for a short break to avoid fatigue. If you get drowsy, pull over safely and take a nap or get a room for the night.

questions.question: What is a blind spot?

options.text: An area you cannot see without turning your head.
The area directly behind your vehicle.
The area you see in your rearview mirror.
The area you see in your side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: An area you cannot see without turning your head.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas next to and behind your vehicle that you cannot see without turning your head.

questions.question: What is used on some highways to direct drivers into the correct turning lanes?

options.text: Flashing red lights
Flashing yellow lights
White lines on the side of the road
White arrows painted in the lanes

questions.correctAnswerText: White arrows painted in the lanes
questions.explanation: Arrows show drivers which lanes to use for going straight or turning.

questions.question: When does Florida law require you to use headlights?

options.text: To get the attention of nearby vehicles.
During the day when it is clear.
Between sunset and sunrise.
When you are feeling tired.

questions.correctAnswerText: Between sunset and sunrise.
questions.explanation: Florida law requires headlights between sunset and sunrise. Drive carefully at night.

questions.question: You hear a siren but cannot see the emergency vehicle. What should you do?

options.text: Keep driving until you see the vehicle.
Pull to the curb and look to see if the vehicle is on your street.
Slow down and don't stop until you see it.
Speed up and turn at the next intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the curb and look to see if the vehicle is on your street.
questions.explanation: If you hear a siren but don't know where the emergency vehicle is, safely pull to the right side of the road and stop until you are sure it is not coming toward you.

questions.question: How should you safely pass a bicycle?

options.text: Honk to let the bicyclist know you are passing.
Drive in the bicycle lane to get a chance to pass.
Slow down and give as much space as possible.
Rush ahead to get in front of the bicyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and give as much space as possible.
questions.explanation: Slow down and give bicyclists as much space as you can. They have less protection than cars and passing too quickly can cause them to lose control.

questions.question: How can you avoid making emergency stops while driving in traffic?

options.text: Honk your horn to warn other drivers.
Look ahead and stay a safe distance behind other cars.
Drive only in the right lane.
Drive slower than the traffic around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead and stay a safe distance behind other cars.
questions.explanation: A safe following distance gives you time to react to problems ahead without sudden stops. This protects you and prevents cars behind you from crashing into you.

questions.question: When driving near a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, you should:

options.text: Slow down and be ready to stop.
Take the right-of-way.
Drive normally.
Drive away quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: When you see a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, slow down and yield the right-of-way. Be ready to stop to keep them safe.

questions.question: What should you do when entering a roadway from a private driveway?

options.text: Honk your horn to warn drivers.
Stop with part of your car on the roadway to alert drivers.
Drive out fast to merge smoothly.
Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and traffic on the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and traffic on the roadway.
questions.explanation: When entering a roadway from a driveway or private road, you must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and all traffic on the roadway.

questions.question: When crossing railroad tracks without signals or gates, you should:

options.text: You have the right-of-way and do not need to check for trains.
You may pass slower drivers while crossing.
Make sure your vehicle can cross the entire track without stopping.
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure your vehicle can cross the entire track without stopping.
questions.explanation: Before driving onto railroad tracks, check that you have enough space to cross completely without stopping. Never pass another vehicle at a railroad crossing. Always look for trains before crossing any tracks.

questions.question: A driver convicted of three traffic accidents over three years must:

options.text: Complete an approved driver improvement course.
Turn in their license.
Not drive on freeways.
Not leave the state.

questions.correctAnswerText: Complete an approved driver improvement course.
questions.explanation: The Three Crashes in Three Years Law requires drivers with three traffic convictions causing accidents within 36 months to complete an approved driver improvement course. They must also take behind-the-wheel training from a driving school and pass an extended test. This must be done within 90 days or their license will be canceled.

questions.question: On long trips, how can you prevent drowsiness?

options.text: Turn on the radio.
Slow down.
Stop regularly to rest and stretch.
Move your eyes side to side while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop regularly to rest and stretch.
questions.explanation: Take regular breaks on long trips. Stop to rest and stretch, even if you do not feel tired.

questions.question: What must you do at a red traffic light?

options.text: Stop at the stop line.
Stop before entering any crosswalk.
Stop before entering the intersection.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: A red light means you must stop before entering the intersection. You must stop at the stop line and before entering any crosswalk.

questions.question: At an intersection with a yield sign, you should:

options.text: Always stop before entering.
Yield only to traffic on the right.
Yield only to traffic on the left.
Slow down and yield the right-of-way to other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and yield the right-of-way to other traffic.
questions.explanation: A yield sign means slow down and let other traffic go first before you enter the intersection or roadway.

questions.question: Driving too slowly is:

options.text: Against the law.
Safe for drivers who are not confident.
What tired drivers should do.
Recommended by police officers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Against the law.
questions.explanation: Driving too slowly is illegal in Florida. Do not drive so slowly that you block or delay traffic moving at normal, safe speeds. Drive with the flow of traffic and within the speed limit.

questions.question: If a car has high beams pointed at you, look toward the ____ of the road.

options.text: Either side
Center
Right side
Left side

questions.correctAnswerText: Right side
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road when a car has high beams aimed at you. This keeps you from being blinded and lets you see the road well enough to stay in your lane until the car passes.

questions.question: Traffic signals sometimes show arrows to control turns from certain lanes. What does a solid red arrow mean?

options.text: It is never used as a traffic signal.
It means the same thing as a red circular traffic light.
It means drivers may turn in the direction the arrow points.
It means traffic in that direction must stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means the same thing as a red circular traffic light.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same thing as a red circular traffic light. You must stop and cannot turn in the direction the arrow points.

questions.question: When can you park or stop on the freeway shoulder?

options.text: As long as you turn on your emergency flashers.
If no part of your vehicle is on the road.
If you need to check a map for directions.
Only in an emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only in an emergency.
questions.explanation: You cannot park on a freeway shoulder except during an emergency.

questions.question: What can a leaking exhaust system do?

options.text: Cause your car to use too much oil.
Make your car need a tune-up sooner.
Make you feel sleepy while driving.
Start grass fires on country roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make you feel sleepy while driving.
questions.explanation: The exhaust system removes toxic gases from your engine. Fumes from a leaky exhaust system are dangerous and can make you drowsy while driving.

questions.question: There is an oncoming car to your left and a bicyclist to your right. What should you do?

options.text: Pull onto the shoulder.
Go between both of them.
Let the car pass, then pass the bicyclist.
Pass the bicyclist quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the car pass, then pass the bicyclist.
questions.explanation: Handle one hazard at a time. Let the oncoming car pass first, then pass the bicyclist. Do not try to squeeze between both at the same time.

questions.question: It starts to rain while you are driving. What should you do?

options.text: Drive faster than the traffic around you.
Drive at the maximum posted speed limit.
Slow down.
Drive very close behind the car in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: When it rains, slow down. Turn on your headlights so others can see you. If the rain is very heavy and you cannot see clearly, pull onto the shoulder and stop until it improves.

questions.question: If you see this sign above your lane, what should you do?

options.text: You cannot exit the freeway.
You can either continue through or exit from your current lane.
You can stay in your lane and continue through.
You must exit if you stay in your current lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must exit if you stay in your current lane.
questions.explanation: An "Exit only" sign means your lane ends at an exit ramp. You can change lanes to continue, or you must exit the freeway if you stay in your current lane.

questions.question: Before changing lanes, what should you check?

options.text: Your side mirror.
Your rearview mirror.
Quickly look over your shoulder for other vehicles.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Check both your side and rearview mirrors for vehicles behind you. Then look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before moving into the other lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop sign ahead.
Lane closed ahead.
Railroad crossing ahead.
Traffic signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. This sign warns that a traffic signal is coming up. Be ready to stop for a yellow or red light.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Keep driving at your current speed.
You must stop ahead.
Speeding is not allowed.
A traffic signal is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A traffic signal is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a traffic signal is ahead.

questions.question: What does drinking coffee after drinking alcohol do?

options.text: Lowers your blood alcohol level.
Removes the effects of alcohol.
Does not change your blood alcohol level.
Raises your blood alcohol level.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not change your blood alcohol level.
questions.explanation: Coffee will not lower your blood alcohol level. It may help you stay awake, but it cannot make you sober or change your blood alcohol level.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Side road.
Stay on the side shown by the arrow.
You can drive in the left lane.
You have the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay on the side shown by the arrow.
questions.explanation: This is a "Keep right" sign. It warns that a traffic island, median, or barrier is ahead. You must keep to the right of it.

questions.question: A pedestrian starts to cross in front of your vehicle. What should you do?

options.text: Flash your lights.
Slow down.
Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian cross.
questions.explanation: Always slow down and be ready to stop when you see pedestrians on or crossing the road. Be extra careful around children. Always give pedestrians the right-of-way when they are in a crosswalk.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Sharp turn ahead; slow down.
Work crew ahead.
Side road.
Playground ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sharp turn ahead; slow down.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions and dangers. This sign warns that a sharp turn is coming and you should reduce your speed.

questions.question: Why is it important to watch for motorcycles?

options.text: They are harder to see than cars.
They rarely use their headlights.
Motorcycle riders are less skilled than other drivers.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are harder to see than cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are small and easy to miss. They can hide in your blind spot. It is hard to judge how far away a motorcycle is and how fast it is going. Always be alert and careful around motorcycles.

questions.question: When you want to make a right turn, where should your car be?

options.text: Near the center of the street.
Close to the left side of the street.
Close to the right side of the street.
Past the center of the intersection when you begin to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close to the right side of the street.
questions.explanation: Get as far to the right side of the road as possible before turning right. Do not cut across other lanes to make any turn.

questions.question: A fully loaded tractor-trailer going 55 mph might need up to ____ feet to stop completely.
questions.explanation: Tractor-trailers need more distance to stop than smaller cars at the same speed. A fully loaded tractor-trailer may need about 400 feet to stop when traveling at 55 mph.

questions.question: When can you go through a stop sign intersection that has no stop line or crosswalk?

options.text: After slowing down to check that there is no cross traffic
After coming to a complete stop and checking that it is safe
After stopping at least 20 feet before the intersection
After slowing down to 10 mph

questions.correctAnswerText: After coming to a complete stop and checking that it is safe
questions.explanation: Stop before the stop line or crosswalk at any stop sign. If there is no stop line or crosswalk, stop before entering the intersection. Then proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: If you are driving slowly and traffic is backing up behind you, what should you do?

options.text: Drive even slower.
Pull over to the right side and let traffic pass.
Do not let other cars pass you.
Use your four-way flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the right side and let traffic pass.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic is dangerous. On a two-lane road, if traffic is backing up behind you, you must pull off the road and let the other vehicles pass. Only drive slowly when road conditions require it.

questions.question: When two cars arrive at an intersection at the same time with no signs or signals, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The car coming from the right.
The car coming from the left.
The car whose driver honks first.
The car traveling fastest.

questions.correctAnswerText: The car coming from the right.
questions.explanation: At an intersection without traffic signs or signals, you must yield to the vehicle coming from your right.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Road widens ahead.
The right lane ends soon.
Highway entrance ramp ahead.
The left lane ends soon.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane ends soon.
questions.explanation: This sign means the right lane is ending.
